newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Large Telebras spreads on AMEX.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Large Telebras spreads on AMEX.

text.p: A couple of sizable spreads were seen in options on American Depositary Receipts of Brazil's Telebras Friday, traders said.
On the American Stock Exchange, the Telebras February 90 call traded about 7,800 contracts and the February 85 put traded 6,105.
The call ended up 3/8 at 1 and the put finished down 7/16 at 1-1/16.
"A large customer sold the puts and bought the calls," a trader at the American Stock Exchange said. "It's kind of bizarre, but that's what happened."
He called the strategy a reverse collar and said it was most likely done by an investor long the stock.
Telebras shares in the U.S. finished 1-1/8 higher at 87-1/4.
Another spread was seen in the Telebras March 85 and March 90 calls, each of which traded about 1,500 contracts. The spread was done in four blocks, two each of 1,000 contracts and 500 contracts.
In other trading, options on Mercury Finance Co began trading along with the stock for the first time since Tuesday.
The company said Wednesday it had restated its earnings for the past four years because of accounting irregularities, lowering earnings by about $90 million.
On Friday, it said it would be unable to pay $17 million in commercial debt due the same day.
The stock fell 12-3/4 points to 2-1/8 on more than 42 million shares in consolidated trading.
The Mercury August five call traded about 3,340 contracts. The option was a new listing and so had zero open interest. It finished at 1/2 after trading between 1/16 and 3/4.
One trader said that with the option priced so low, investors were taking a relatively low-risk bet that the shares would recover the $5 level by the August expiration.
Other active Mercury options included the March five call, the May five call and even the February five call.
The February five call traded about 250 contracts, closing at 3/16. It traded in a tight band between 1/16 and 3/16. It also was a new listing.
The February five put was the most active Mercury put, with volume of 115 contracts. That option ended at 2-7/8 after bouncing between 2-3/4 and 3-3/8.
Elsewhere, traders said put buying in Philip Morris Cos Inc increased as the stock retreated. Philip Morris shares eased a point to 118-7/8 on consolidated volume of about 3.6 million.
The busiest Philip Morris put was the June 110, with volume of about 4,715 contracts. The option had open interest of 4,802, which included an addition of 3,388 contracts Thursday.
Other busy puts in the group included the June 120, the June 100 and the March 110. The June 120 call traded 5,180. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
